description:
FILED s399 as the residue of #314 family F-D (whose SCALAR half shipped in
s399e).  Both halves below are CONTAINER spans across a package boundary, they
have DIFFERENT causes, and NEITHER is "the facts scan does not record container
declarations" -- `container_decl` and its own span loop (W10-ext-3) have
existed since s305.  Measured, do not re-derive.

--- (b1) a file with MORE THAN ONE `my @x` cannot promote either ------------

op/svleak.t dies `my-lexical 'a' (canon @a) spans a package boundary`.  The
container loop's second line is

    next unless ($f->{canon_decl_count}{$csym} // 0) == 1;   # sole binding

and svleak.t declares `my @a` three times (line 67 file-level, 147
`tie my @a, 'main'` inside a block, 174 inside another block).  The rule is
deliberate and its comment says why: the promotion lowers the decl to a
defvar'd cell, and "a nested `let @x` under the defvar'd special is the poison
the file-uniqueness rule exists to prevent".

WHAT MIGHT LIFT IT: direction D changed the ground under that comment -- a
`let` of a symbol-macro name is LEGAL CL and SHADOWS it (that IS the my-shadow
mechanism, [[project global-cell]] / Pl/t/global-cell-01.t).  So the question
is whether the poison still exists for a p-defcell container.  MEASURE THAT
FIRST (a hand-written CL probe against the runtime is enough); if it does not,
the rule can become "sole binding at THIS extent" like the scalar loop's, which
is the same shape M-B gave the scalars.
ZERO rows behind it: svleak.t then needs XS::APItest's sv_count (measured s396,
unreachable).  So this is a decline on ordinary Perl, not a row count.

--- (b2) a container NAME INSIDE a list declaration --------------------------

    my ($x, @rest) = (1, 2, 3);
    package Qux; sub readmix { "$x:@rest" }
    package main; print Qux::readmix();
        perl: 1:2 3        PCL: Parser2 TODO: my-lexical 'rest' (canon @rest)
                                spans a package boundary

The scalar name `$x` is handled since s399e.  `mlist_decl` ALREADY carries the
`[$decl, '@rest']` pair the container loop wants, so the loop's *analysis* half
needs only the same merge s399e did for scalars -- but the loop marks the decl
with `_file_lex_renamed{$csym}` and the DECL LOWERING that consumes that mark
(`_lower_block`'s no-init single-container branch) knows only `my @a;`.  A list
decl arriving there is a shape it has never seen, and it has an INITIALIZER,
which that branch also excludes.  So the fix is the lowering half, not the
facts half; size it there.

Occurs in NO measured file (perl-tests, perl's t/, board14, lib) -- found by a
guard-row probe.  It is a filler.

BAR for either half: probe ~10 shapes vs perl (both sigils, with and without
init, a sibling same-name scalar, a nested shadow in a block, interpolated
"@rest" in a later package, `$#rest`, a slice); the s372 two-population
GATE-SET scan (tools/gate-set-scan.pl, ~2.5 min per population:
638 files, first stderr line, normalized); corpus-diff; gate; and the full
sweep, because it is a name-resolution change (the #296 rule).


RULED s401 (docs/fable-answers-s400.md Â§5): unscheduled filler behind the
release track (zero rows, but a decline on ordinary Perl).  b1's fix SHAPE:
DELETE the container loop's file-uniqueness rule if direction D ("a `let` of
a symbol-macro name is legal CL and shadows it") makes it unnecessary â the
comment justifying the rule predates D; measured at the s372 gate-SET bar
over both populations.  b2 is a separate half-session; do not fold them.
subject: #314 F-D residue: a CONTAINER spanning a package boundary — (b1) a file with >1 `my @x` refuses (canon-uniqueness rule), (b2) a container name inside a list decl refuses (decl lowering)
